artifacts.synopsis: TE David Senters complained that Savannah River Presbytery erred by judging TE Stamberg's stated difference with WCF 21.3 regarding the gift of tongues as 'not a difference' during a transfer examination. The SJC denied the procedural part of the complaint but sustained the confessional part, finding it was error to conclude Stamberg's view on continuing tongues was not a difference with WCF 1.1 and 1.6, and remanded to Presbytery for further action.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.

artifacts.synopsis: Heartland Presbytery sustained the transfer of TE Geoff Smith from an OPC presbytery with stated differences on WCF 19 (the law), without adequately considering or disclosing to the full presbytery that the OPC had declared Smith's views outside the system of doctrine and had restricted him from teaching them. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded to Heartland for further action, with a dissent arguing there was no clear error under BCO 39-3(3).

artifacts.title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred in granting TE Hickey an exception to Larger Catechism 177 regarding admission of covenant children to the Lord's Supper. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint, remanding the case to the Presbytery because the record was insufficient to evaluate the minister's particular expression of his paedocommunion view.
